methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates a pooled base-editing screen with orthogonal validation (synthetic sgRNA single-edits, Sanger/EditR, amplicon NGS, single-cell DNA haplotyping), multiple in vitro functional assays, in vivo xenograft models with rechallenge, scRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq, metabolomics and Seahorse flux analysis — a comprehensive and rigorous preclinical pipeline. Replication is addressed through two donors in the screen, up to 16 biologically independent donors in follow-up assays, two CAR scFv contexts (CD19, B7H3, L1CAM) and corroboration in patient-derived T cells. Statistical analyses are appropriate per assay (paired t-tests when within-donor paired, Wilcoxon when normality fails per Shapiro–Wilk, one-sample tests for normalized values, Mantel–Cox for survival), with pre-specified cutoffs for the screen (≥0.4% start-point frequency, fold-change over baseline). Weaknesses explicitly reported include: no a priori power calculation, no blinding for in vitro work, blinded tumor burden measurement but non-blinded analysis, and scRNA-seq from a single donor. No formal multiplicity correction is described for the pooled screen beyond the dual-donor consistency check, and effect sizes/CIs are not consistently reported alongside p-values.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical mechanistic and therapeutic-development study using primary human T cells and NSG xenograft models, mapping to Oxford LoE 5. Despite the low LoE, the clinical/translational relevance is high: ROADSTAR offers a generalizable, CAR-design-matched base-editing strategy that could directly inform next-generation clinical CAR T cell manufacturing, including hematologic (Nalm6/CD19) and solid-tumor (neuroblastoma/B7H3, L1CAM) indications. Translational credibility is reinforced by validation in T cells from heavily pretreated patients with cancer, direct safety assessment (no lymphomagenesis, no CRS-like cytokine signature, intact organ histology up to 66 days), and the use of clinically relevant endpoints (survival, functional persistence, rechallenge). The findings are not yet practice-changing without first-in-human data but constitute a clear preclinical foundation for IND-enabling work.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE is the appropriate checklist given primary reliance on NSG xenograft experiments. The manuscript reports species/strain, sex, age, housing, approvals (Regierungspräsidium Tübingen; IACUC Zhejiang; and human ethics 783/2023BO2, 846/2020BO2), randomization after tumor-burden equalization, blinded tumor burden measurement, humane endpoints, exclusion criteria, and sample sizes per group with donor counts. Minor gaps: no formal sample-size justification or power calculation, blinding only partial, and biosafety/husbandry details are modest. Data availability is strong — Zenodo deposits are cited for scRNA-seq (17293317), bulk RNA-seq (17292714), and metabolomics (17426175); public tools (Galaxy, Scanpy, Cell Ranger, STAR, Salmon, DESeq2, nf-core/rnaseq, MetaboAnalyst) with versions are reported — though custom pysam filtering and some pipeline code have redacted repository links in the blinded text, so independent code access cannot be verified here.

novelty_literature.justification: The core conceptual advance — matching endogenous signaling perturbations to specific CAR costimulatory domains (28z vs BBz) via base editing (ROADSTAR) — is novel and well-positioned, demonstrating that the same PIK3CD mutation (E81K) is beneficial in BBz but detrimental in 28z CARs while a different mutation (L32P) benefits 28z. The authors appropriately cite the directly comparable prior PIK3CD base-editing screens in untransduced T cells (Schmidt et al., 2024; Walsh et al., 2025), credibly arguing those approaches would miss CAR-context-dependent effects. Methodological novelty is incremental (base-editing screens in T cells and CAR engineering are each established), but the integration into CAR-specific signaling calibration, the discovery of divergent beneficial alleles per costimulatory domain, and the mechanistic depth (scRNA-seq, metabolomics, Seahorse) collectively amount to a meaningful empirical and conceptual advance beyond prior art.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written, well-structured and uses consistent terminology; acronyms (ABD, CBE/ABE, pAKT, SCM, EM) are introduced appropriately. The abstract is self-contained and quantitatively accurate; the introduction effectively motivates the ROADSTAR hypothesis and locates it against prior CAR-signaling optimization work. Figure captions are highly informative with explicit n, statistical tests, biological independence, and E:T ratios. The discussion is appropriately scoped, acknowledges the APDS context, and addresses the safety concern directly. Minor issues include dense methods paragraphs that could be tightened and some redundancy between the Main and Discussion sections regarding ROADSTAR framing.

key_strengths: CAR-design-matched base-editing concept (ROADSTAR) revealing divergent beneficial PIK3CD alleles (E81K for BBz, L32P for 28z) is conceptually novel and well-controlled with two-donor screen replication plus positive (RASA2) and neutral (CD19) sgRNA controls

Comprehensive mechanistic validation integrating phosphoflow, bulk and scRNA-seq, untargeted/targeted metabolomics, Seahorse flux and single-cell DNA haplotyping to establish on-target specificity and functional pathway effects

In vivo rigor across multiple xenograft models (Nalm6 CD19, Sh-Sy5y B7H3 and L1CAM neuroblastoma) with tumor rechallenge, long-term follow-up to day 66, and direct safety readouts (histology, liver enzymes, cytokines, lymphomagenesis assessment)
Translational credibility reinforced by replication in T cells from heavily pretreated patients with cancer and by anchoring E81K biology to the human APDS literature
Strong data deposition posture — Zenodo repositories for scRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq and metabolomics; versioned public tools throughout
key_concerns: No a priori power/sample-size calculation; blinding is partial (tumor burden acquisition blinded but analysis not), and no blinding for in vitro work
scRNA-seq is from a single donor, limiting generalizability of cluster-level claims (e.g., metabolically active CD4+ cluster uniquely enriched by E81K)
Statistical reporting leans on p-values without consistent effect-size/CI reporting; no formal multiplicity correction described for the pooled screen beyond dual-donor concordance
Safety claim rests on 66-day follow-up in NSG mice and cBioPortal absence of E81K/L32P in T-cell leukemias — adequate for preclinical but not definitive for malignant-transformation risk assessment
Patient-derived T cell experiments are described broadly (sarcoma, lung, breast; n not detailed in all panels) and could benefit from clearer disease-level breakdown
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a conceptually novel, mechanistically deep, and clinically oriented preclinical CAR T engineering study with rigorous multi-modal validation and strong data sharing. The combination of a credibly novel framework (CAR-context-specific signaling calibration via base editing), convincing in vivo efficacy with explicit safety assessment, and depth of mechanism supports Tier 1 placement with minor revisions.
